content: Phentermine is a medication prescribed to aid in weight loss when used in conjunction with a proper diet and exercise regimen. It functions by suppressing appetite. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Phentermine is available in tablet form and as extended-release capsules. It is typically taken as a single daily dose in the morning or three times a day, 30 minutes before meals. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take phentermine exactly as directed. Most individuals use this medication for a duration of 3 to 6 weeks, depending on their response to treatment. Phentermine has the potential to be habit-forming, so do not take a larger dose, take it more frequently, or use it for a longer period than prescribed by your doctor. To minimize side effects, phentermine should be taken with meals. If you are using an extended-release product, do not chew or crush the tablet. Some tablets, however, may be crushed and mixed with food—consult your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Before taking phentermine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to phentermine or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially fluoxetine (Prozac), fluvoxamine (Luvox), guanethidine, insulin, MAO inhibitors (even if discontinued within the past two weeks), medications for weight loss or depression, paroxetine (Paxil), sertraline (Zoloft), and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had heart disease, high blood pressure, arteriosclerosis (narrowing of the arteries), hyperthyroidism (overactive thyroid gland), diabetes, glaucoma, or a history of drug abuse. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking phentermine, contact your doctor immediately. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can exacerbate the drowsiness caused by this drug. If you have diabetes, you may require a higher dose of insulin while taking phentermine. Contact your doctor if you have any questions or concerns. Follow the diet and exercise program prescribed by your doctor. Phentermine is most effective when combined with a structured diet plan. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Phentermine may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following mild symptoms, especially if they persist or worsen: dry mouth, unpleasant taste, diarrhea, constipation, or vomiting. If you experience any severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately. These may include increased blood pressure, heart palpitations, restlessness, dizziness, tremor, insomnia, shortness of breath, chest pain, swelling of the legs and ankles, or difficulty performing physical activities you were previously able to do. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will order specific lab tests to monitor your response to phentermine. Do not share this medication with anyone else. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
